nodes.description: Because the pathway stalls, the truncated species Dol-PP-GlcNAc2Man5 accumulates intracellularly while the cytosolic free oligosaccharide GlcNAc2Man5 is absent. This paired pattern is the biochemical signature that first identified the defect and mirrors the profile of RFT1-null yeast.

evidence.reference_title: Human RFT1 deficiency leads to a disorder of N-linked glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: RFT1 deficiency in both yeast and human cells leads to the accumulation of incomplete DolPP-GlcNAc(2)Man(5) and to a profound glycosylation disorder in humans.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive description of the phenotype of the first case of congenital disorder of glycosylation due to RFT1 deficiency (CDG In).
evidence.snippet: Accumulation of intracellular DolPP-GlcNAc(2)Man(5) with absence of cytosolic GlcNAc(2)Man(5) resembled the profile of a yeast mutant deficient in RFT1, a protein that is thought to have a role as a flippase.

nodes.description: Assembly of the N-glycosylation donor is a two-compartment process: the Man5GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol intermediate is built on the cytosolic face of the ER and must reach the lumen for the remaining mannose and glucose residues to be added. In RFT1 deficiency this transition fails, and the pathway stalls at the Man5 intermediate. The step itself is not in doubt; what RFT1 actually does at this step is, and the two readings are curated as competing hypotheses below.

evidence.reference_title: Human RFT1 deficiency leads to a disorder of N-linked glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: The substrate of N-linked glycosylation, dolichol pyrophosphate (DolPP)-GlcNAc(2)Man(9)Glc(3), is assembled through a complex series of ordered reactions requiring the translocation of the intermediate DolPP-GlcNAc(2)Man(5) structure across the endoplasmic-reticulum membrane.

evidence.reference_title: RFT1-CDG: deafness as a novel feature of congenital disorders of glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: RFT1 is involved in the transfer of Man(5)GlcNAc(2)-PP-Dol from the cytoplasmic to the luminal side of the endoplasmic reticulum.

nodes.description: Because N-glycosylation is required by a very large and functionally diverse set of secreted and membrane proteins, hypoglycosylation produces disease in many organs at once. In RFT1-CDG the burden falls most heavily on the nervous system and the ear: drug-resistant early-onset epilepsy, profound developmental impairment and visual failure, together with the sensorineural deafness that distinguishes this CDG from the others. Coagulation-factor hypoglycosylation adds a bleeding-and-thrombosis diathesis that proved fatal in the index case.

evidence.reference_title: RFT1-CDG: deafness as a novel feature of congenital disorders of glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: Remarkably, all six patients with RFT1-CDG show sensorineural deafness as part of a severe neurological syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive description of the phenotype of the first case of congenital disorder of glycosylation due to RFT1 deficiency (CDG In).
evidence.snippet: The patient showed very little development and no vision and suffered from drug-resistant epilepsy.

nodes.description: With the mature donor unavailable, the oligosaccharyltransferase reaction proceeds at reduced efficiency and sequons on nascent glycoproteins are left unoccupied. Site occupancy, rather than glycan structure, is what falls — which is why the defect presents biochemically as a CDG type I pattern on serum transferrin isoelectric focusing.

evidence.reference_title: RFT1 deficiency in three novel CDG patients.
evidence.snippet: The pathogenic character of the novel mutations was illustrated by the accumulation of Man(5)GlcNAc(2)-PP-dolichol and by reduced recombinant DNase 1 secretion.

evidence.reference_title: RFT1 deficiency in three novel CDG patients.
evidence.snippet: Both the glycosylation pattern and recombinant DNase 1 secretion could be normalized by expression of normal RFT1 cDNA in the patients' fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital disorders of glycosylation: an update on defects affecting the biosynthesis of dolichol-linked oligosaccharides.
evidence.snippet: Defects in the biosynthesis of the oligosaccharide precursor for N-glycosylation lead to decreased occupancy of glycosylation sites and thereby to diseases known as congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG).

evidence.reference_title: RFT1 deficiency in three novel CDG patients.
evidence.snippet: The first patient was homozygous for the earlier reported RFT1 missense mutation (c.199C>T; p.R67C), whereas the two other patients were homozygous for the missense mutation c.454A>G (p.K152E) and c.892G>A (p.E298 K), respectively.

evidence.reference_title: RFT1 deficiency in three novel CDG patients.
evidence.snippet: All three RFT1 mutations identified so far are located in one of the hydrophilic loops predicted to be within the ER lumen.

evidence.reference_title: RFT1 deficiency in three novel CDG patients.
evidence.snippet: This could thus point to a founder effect of the p.R67C mutation.

meta.frequency: All reported patients (biallelic in every case)

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic RFT1 variants reduce or abolish the function of RFT1, a multispanning ER membrane protein whose N and C termini both face the cytoplasm. The index allele, c.199C>T (p.Arg67Cys), was shown to be functionally deleterious by complementation assay in RFT1-null yeast, and most RFT1-CDG alleles reported since fall in regions of the protein that are highly conserved across eukaryotes.

evidence.reference_title: Human RFT1 deficiency leads to a disorder of N-linked glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: Despite the low sequence similarity between the yeast and the human RFT1 proteins, we demonstrated both their functional orthology and the pathologic effect of the human p.R67C mutation by complementation assay in Deltarft1 yeast cells.

evidence.snippet: We show that it is a multispanning membrane protein located in the ER, with its N and C termini facing the cytoplasm.

genetic_context.description: Reported genotypes are biallelic germline RFT1 variants, homozygous in the index case. Loss of function is established functionally: the index allele failed to complement RFT1-null yeast, and wild-type RFT1 cDNA restored normal glycosylation in patient fibroblasts.
